text:
anya: heads up — p99 TTFT for model=neo-1 @ eu-west-1 jumped from ~180ms to ~520ms around 12:34 UTC. tokens/sec also spiked. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abcd/token-slo?orgId=1
sam: saw that. alert fired?
alerts-bot: [FIRING] token_ttft_p99_high (env=prod, region=eu-west-1, model=neo-1) — value=520ms, threshold=400ms, since=2026-03-10T12:36:15Z
marco: can we slice by shard and gpu_pool? want to see if it's a single hotshard or general queuing
lisa: also check kvcache hit rate — if cache miss rate rose, ttft goes up with long prefixes
sam: quick promql to split by shard/gpu_pool:```sum by (shard, gpu_pool) (rate(inference_token_latency_seconds_bucket{job="inference"}[5m]))``` then use `histogram_quantile(0.99, ...)` on that for p99
anya: thanks. i ran a quick query and p99 is dominated by shard=hot-23, gpu_pool=dedicated-eu1. tokens/sec for that shard doubled. looks like a batching bump from a noisy client
marco: noisy neighbor then. any network errors on that host?```sum by (instance) (increase(node_network_receive_errs_total[5m]))``` returned zeros
lisa: KV cache hitrate for hot-23 dropped from 92% -> 68% at the same time. suspect prefix pattern changed — client sent longer unique prompts so cache ineffective
san: (note) if caching improvement isn't quick, we'll hit more per-token cost and sustained SLO violations. we should avoid alarm storms by tuning alert to require tokens/sec > 1000 && p99 > 400ms for 5m
anya: agreed. current alert is just p99 > 400ms for 2m which is noisy for short bursts
marco: propose new alert rule (Grafana alert) — combine rate and p99:```expr: (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, model, region) (rate(inference_token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) ) > 0.4) and (sum by (model, region) (rate(inference_tokens_count_total[5m])) > 1000)``` eval_interval: 1m for firing, for_resolve: 10m
lisa: please also add annotation with `top_shard` helper:```topk(1, sum by (shard) (rate(inference_tokens_count_total{model="neo-1"}[5m])))``` so alert links to the shard causing the spike
anya: action plan: 1) short term - silence/raise alert noise window and add shard annotation (sam) 2) mid term - add per-shard heatmap panel and topk link (marco) 3) long term - tune batching and caching recommendations for SDK clients, update docs (ops + devex)
sam: i'll push alert change in 10m, PR link when ready
marco: i'll add a per-shard heatmap to the token-slo dashboard and include a filter for `gpu_pool` and `model`
lisa: i'll reach out to the customer (via support) for client prompt pattern. cc: @support-team
deploy-bot: Started rollout of grafana-alerts v2.3.1 to prod (change: token_ttft_p99_high updated) — rollout id r-20260310-01
anya: thanks. also, can we add cost estimate to the panel? e.g. per-shard tokens/sec * $/token to see immediate cost impact when caches miss
sam: yes — i'll add a small stat panel: `sum(rate(inference_tokens_count_total[5m])) by (shard) * 0.000002` (placeholder $/token)
anya: perfect. after change lands, we'll monitor for 30m and decide if we need to cordon hot-23 and move workloads or increase reserved capacity briefly
marco: FYI i already prepared a kubectl drain cmd for the node behind hot-23 if we need quick relief:```kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-023 && kubectl drain node/gpu-node-023 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force```
lisa: +1. will hold until we see sustained degradation
anya: closing loop — thanks everyone. will post post-mortem if this turns into a longer incident. :thumbsup:
